finalists.label: Fetal Brain Disruption Sequence
finalists.why: It has the most specific for evidence, including fetal MRI findings and ex vacuo enlargement of the right lateral ventricle.

finalists.label: Intracranial hemorrhage
finalists.why: It has strong for evidence, including fetal ultrasound and MRI findings, with no against evidence.

finalists.label: Porencephaly
finalists.why: It has strong for evidence, including fetal ultrasound, MRI, and cranial ultrasound findings, with no against evidence.

frontier_selector.why: Fetal Brain Disruption Sequence is chosen because it accounts for the most decisive findings in the vignette, including the porencephalic cyst, ex vacuo enlargement of the right lateral ventricle, and abnormal micropolygyria of the right frontal cortex.

support_spans: fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks suggested intracranial hemorrhage
fetal MRI at 25 weeks, which showed a 2.3 cm porencephalic cyst in the right frontotemporal–insular region
Cranial ultrasound on day 1 showed a right porencephalic area with “ex vacuo” enlargement of the right lateral ventricle and a germinolytic cyst on the left
contradict_spans: maternal febrile episode occurred in the periconceptional period; there was no trauma, and no use of cocaine, warfarin, or anticonvulsants
